content:
One of the most frustrating things about the iPhone user interface is that we have to guess to change an app's settings.

Sometimes we'll open the app itself and go into its built-in settings menu. But other times, we have to leave that app and open another completely separate Apple "Settings" app. Honestly, this experience is pretty awkward (though there's a free shortcut that can help)...

The "Settings" Problem

We've all been through this. You want to change an app's settings, so you go to the "hamburger menu," choose "Settings," and look for what you want to change. Turns out you can't find it, and only then realize you have to leave this app, open Apple's "Settings" app, find that app, make the change there, and finally reopen the app you wanted to use.

The process itself is already awkward enough, but even worse is that from the start, we have to guess where to look.

Take Apple's "Camera" app as an example. Recent iPhones offer what Apple calls a "Fusion Camera" for the 1x lens. The default is 24mm, but we can actually change the default to 28mm or 35mm. How it works is that the app automatically applies a crop effect. In addition, we can also choose whether we need to tap the "1x" button to cycle through different focal lengths.

However, unless there's some hidden location I haven't discovered, there's no way to do this directly within the "Camera" app. Instead, we have to open the "Settings" app, find "Camera"*, scroll down to the "Photo Capture" section, tap "Fusion Camera"—only then can we get to where we can choose.

*And I haven't even mentioned another thing: you also have to guess whether an Apple app will have its own dedicated category in "Settings," or whether it'll be grouped under "Apps"...

A Partial Workaround with Shortcuts

There's no way to completely avoid the guessing game, but at least there's a third-party shortcut made by Quinn Nelson from Snazzy Labs that can help ease the pain a little.

Thanks to John Gruber for bringing this shortcut to my attention. If you want to install it yourself:

  • Download and install it here
  • Open "Control Center"
  • Tap the + button in the top left corner
  • Tap "Add a Control" at the bottom
  • Look for "Shortcuts"
  • Tap "Run Shortcut"
  • Choose the "App Settings" shortcut

Once installed, if you're using an app and realize you need to go to another "Settings" app to find the settings, just swipe down from the top right corner to open "Control Center," and then tap the "App Settings" button.

However, Apple Should Properly Address This Issue

What I'd like to see is a comprehensive solution, rather than relying on third-party workarounds.

My suggestion is that at the bottom of each app's settings menu, there should be a "More" option that automatically opens the "Settings" app and jumps to the correct page. That way, if we can't find what we're looking for in the app's internal settings menu, we only need one extra tap.

To be clear, Apple actually already provides an API that can do this, but not many developers use it. I hope Apple can make this a mandatory requirement.

Is there anything you'd like to see? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
